changes.before: Create open_tasks(project_id,task_id) showing every project and only unfinished task matches. Preserve projects and tasks.
changes.after: Choose which tasks match without removing projects that have none.

before: To show every project alongside its unfinished tasks, put t.done=0 inside the LEFT JOIN’s ON condition. That condition decides which right-side rows count as matches. If none qualify, the project still gets a row with NULL right-side columns.

Moving t.done=0 to WHERE changes the question. It filters rows after the join. A finished matched task fails; a NULL-extended task produces NULL rather than true. Both are removed, so projects without an unfinished task disappear. A project with several unfinished tasks can legitimately produce several rows.
Optional practice: add a second unfinished task to Map. Predict why it produces another row instead of replacing task 11.
after: In a LEFT JOIN, `ON` decides which right-side rows count as matches. Put the unfinished-task check there when every project must stay in the result.
If no task passes the ON checks, the project still appears with NULL task columns. A project with two unfinished tasks gets two result rows.
`WHERE t.done = 0` would filter the joined rows afterward. It removes finished tasks and also removes rows where done is NULL. Projects with no unfinished task would disappear.
Create `open_tasks(project_id, task_id)` from the supplied projects and tasks. Keep every project and match only unfinished tasks. Leave both source tables unchanged.
